title: INT truncates toward zero — INT(-2.7) is -2, not -3
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE FLOOR_NEG(X, IFLOOR)
C     Engineer expected this to return mathematical floor(X). It
C     doesn't -- INT truncates toward zero, so INT(-2.7) = -2 (not
C     -3). Translating INT to Java's (int) cast preserves the bug;
C     translating to Math.floor changes the contract.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL    X
      INTEGER IFLOOR
      IFLOOR = INT(X)
      RETURN
      END
notes: Pure F77 INT() truncates; INT(2.7) = 2 and INT(-2.7) = -2. This is asymmetric with FLOOR (which would give -3 for -2.7). Engineers reviewing the port assume 'cast to int' = 'floor' which is true for non-negative reals but wrong for negative. The spec must surface BOTH the truncate-toward-zero semantic AND the open question of which mapping the rewrite should use.
